To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

shell-model calculations using GXPF1a or KB3G interactions reproduce experimental Gamow Teller strength distributions of stable pf-shell nuclei with 45 A<64, and that electron-capture rates estimated with these shell-model calculations deviate less than 30% from those estimated with experimental Gamow-Tellar strength distributions.

shell-model calculations in a pf-model space using the GXPF 1a or KB3G effective interaction can be used to calculate electron-capture rates in pf-shell nuclei with relatively good accuracy, while ground-state electron-capture rate calculations based on the QR-PA formalism discussed here exhibit much larger deviations and should be used cautiously, especially at low densities.

(1) shell-model calculations in pf shell model space with the GXPF1A and KB3G interaction reproduce Gamow-Teller β + strength distributions in the pf shell with a mean absolute deviation from the data of 30% and 47% (respectively), and (2) electron-capture rates calculated from these strength distributions deviate on average by less than 30% from the rates derived from the data for stellar densities in excess 10 7g/cm 3.

shell models with the KB3g and GXPF1 interactions are good for electron-capture rates, and QRPA is not.
shell models are a very good tool for estimating Gamow-Teller distributions and hence electron-capture rates.
shell models are the best available tool for estimating electron-capture rates at stellar conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
shell-model calculations in a large model space can be used as reliable input for electron-capture rate estimates in stellar evolution models.
the shell-model formalism is the most reliable method to calculate electron-capture rates in the pf shell for astrophysical applications.

, for a given nucleus, it is crucial to use the same interaction to calculate both the parent and daughter Gamow-Teller distributions in order to derive electron-capture rates that are free from model-dependent uncertainties.
